original_instruction: How did the narrator describe his grandmother's physical appearance and age?
original_input: My grandmother, like everybody’s grandmother, was an old woman. She had been old and wrinkled for the twenty years that I had known her. ... She had always been short and fat and slightly bent. Her face was a criss-cross of wrinkles running from everywhere to everywhere. No, we were certain she had always been as we had known her. Old, so terribly old that she could not have grown older, and had stayed at the same age for twenty years.
original_output: The narrator described his grandmother as an old woman who had been old and wrinkled for the twenty years he had known her. She was short, fat, slightly bent, and her face was a criss-cross of wrinkles, giving the impression that she had stayed the same terribly old age for two decades.
hinglish_question: Narrator ne apni daadi ki physical appearance aur age kaise describe kiya hai? Yaani, daadi ki umar aur physical appearance kaisi thi?
hinglish_answer: Narrator ne apni daadi ko ek old woman ke roop me describe kiya hai jo 20 saal se old aur wrinkled thi. Vah choti, moti, thodi bent thi aur uske chehre par wrinkles ke nishan the, jisse lagta hai ki vah 20 saal se same umar par thi.

original_instruction: What details are given about the grandfather's portrait?
original_input: My grandfather’s portrait hung above the mantelpiece in the drawing room. He wore a big turban and loose-fitting clothes. His long, white beard covered the best part of his chest and he looked at least a hundred years old. He did not look the sort of person who would have a wife or children. He looked as if he could only have lots and lots of grandchildren.
original_output: The grandfather's portrait hung above the mantelpiece in the drawing room. He was depicted wearing a big turban and loose-fitting clothes, with a long, white beard covering most of his chest. He appeared to be at least a hundred years old and seemed like a person who would only have grandchildren, not a wife or children.
hinglish_question: Dada ji ke portrait ke baare mein kya details diye gaye hain? Mera dada ji ka portrait drawing room mein mantelpiece ke upar laga hua tha. Usne bada sa turban aur loose fitting kapde pehne huye the. Uski lambi, safed daadi uske seene ke adhikansh hisse ko dhak rahi thi aur woh kam se kam 100 saal ka lag raha tha. Usse aisa lagta tha jaise woh wife ya bachchon wala aadmi nahi ho sakta. Usse lagta tha jaise woh sirf bahut saare pote-poti wala aadmi ho sakta hai.
hinglish_answer: Dada ji ka portrait drawing room mein mantelpiece ke upar laga hua tha. Usne bada sa turban aur loose fitting kapde pehne huye the, aur uski lambi, safed daadi uske seene ke adhikansh hisse ko dhak rahi thi. Uski umar kam se kam 100 saal ki lag rahi thi aur usse aisa lagta tha jaise woh sirf bahut saare pote-poti wala aadmi ho sakta hai, wife ya bachchon wala nahi.

original_instruction: Describe the daily morning routine shared by the narrator and his grandmother in the village.
original_input: She used to wake me up in the morning and get me ready for school. She said her morning prayer in a monotonous sing-song while she bathed and dressed me in the hope that I would listen and get to know it by heart; I listened because I loved her voice but never bothered to learn it. Then she would fetch my wooden slate which she had already washed and plastered with yellow chalk, a tiny earthen ink-pot and a red pen, tie them all in a bundle and hand it to me. After a breakfast of a thick, stale chapatti with a little butter and sugar spread on it, we went to school. She carried several stale chapattis with her for the village dogs. My grandmother always went to school with me because the school was attached to the temple.
original_output: In the village, the grandmother would wake the narrator up and get him ready for school, reciting morning prayers while bathing and dressing him. She would prepare his school supplies, including a wooden slate, ink-pot, and pen. After a breakfast of stale chapatti with butter and sugar, they would walk to the school, which was attached to a temple, and she would carry extra chapattis for the village dogs.
hinglish_question: Gaon mein narrator aur uski dadi ki subah ki routine kya thi? Vo mujhe subah uthati thi, mujhe school ke liye taiyar karti thi. Vo apni subah ki prayer ek tarah se gaati thi jab vo mujhe nahaati aur kapde pahnaati thi, ummeed karti thi ki main use sununga aur yaad karunga, lekin main sirf uski awaaz sunne ke liye sunhta tha, use yaad nahin karta tha. Phir vo mera lakdi ka slate lekar aati thi jo vo pehle dho chuki thi aur uspe peela chalk laga chuki thi, ek chhota mitti ka ink-pot aur ek laal pen, sab ko ek bundle mein bandh kar ke mujhe deti thi. Ek moti, purani chapati ke saath thoda makkhan aur cheeni khane ke baad, hum school chale jaate the. Vo gaon ke kutton ke liye kuch purani chapatiyaan bhi le jaati thi. Mere school ka temple ke saath attachment tha, isliye meri dadi hamesha mere saath school jaati thi.
hinglish_answer: Gaon mein, dadi narrator ko uthati thi aur use school ke liye taiyar karti thi, subah ki prayer gaati thi jab vo use nahaati aur kapde pahnaati thi. Vo use lakdi ka slate, ink-pot, aur pen deti thi. Ek moti, purani chapati ke saath thoda makkhan aur cheeni khane ke baad, vo dono school jaate the, jo ek mandir ke saath attached tha, aur vo gaon ke kutton ke liye extra chapatiyaan le jaati thi.

original_instruction: What event marked a 'turning-point' in the narrator's friendship with his grandmother?
original_input: When my parents were comfortably settled in the city, they sent for us. That was a turning-point in our friendship. Although we shared the same room, my grandmother no longer came to school with me. I used to go to an English school in a motor bus. There were no dogs in the streets and she took to feeding sparrows in the courtyard of our city house.
original_output: The 'turning-point' in their friendship occurred when the narrator's parents, after settling in the city, sent for them. From then on, the grandmother no longer accompanied the narrator to school, as he began attending an English school by motor bus, and she started feeding sparrows in their city home's courtyard instead of village dogs.
hinglish_question: Kaun si ghatna thi jisne narrator aur uski daadi ke dosti ko badal diya? Jab meri parents shehar mein settle ho gaye, toh unhone humein bulaya. Woh humari dosti ka ek naya modh tha.
hinglish_answer: Unki dosti ka turning point woh tha jab narrator ke parents ne shehar mein settle hone ke baad unhe bulaya. Uske baad daadi narrator ke school jaane ke liye nahi aati thi, kyunki woh ab english school motor bus se jaata tha, aur daadi ne gaon ke kutte ki jagah shehar ke apne ghar ke aangan mein chidiyon ko khana khilana shuru kar diya tha.

original_instruction: Why was the grandmother unhappy and disturbed by the English school and music lessons?
original_input: This made her unhappy. She could not help me with my lessons. She did not believe in the things they taught at the English school and was distressed that there was no teaching about God and the scriptures. One day I announced that we were being given music lessons. She was very disturbed. To her music had lewd associations. It was the monopoly of harlots and beggars and not meant for gentlefolk.
original_output: The grandmother was unhappy because she couldn't help with the narrator's English school lessons and was distressed that the school taught Western science without including teachings about God and the scriptures. She was particularly disturbed by music lessons, as she associated music with 'lewd associations' and considered it the 'monopoly of harlots and beggars,' not suitable for 'gentlefolk.'
hinglish_question: Dadi ji english school aur music lessons se kyu udas aur pareshan thi? Yeh cheez usse udas karti thi, woh meri lessons mein madad nahi kar sakti thi, aur usse lagta tha ki english school mein jo padhaya ja raha hai woh theek nahi hai, khaskar God aur scriptures ke bare mein kuch nahi sikhaaya ja raha hai. Ek din maine bataya ki humein music lessons di ja rahi hai, toh woh bahut pareshan ho gayi, kyunki usse music ke baare mein galat khayalat the, usse lagta tha ki music sirf randiyon aur bhikariyon ka kaam hai, gentle logon ke liye nahi hai.
hinglish_answer: Dadi ji udas thi kyunki woh english school ke lessons mein meri madad nahi kar sakti thi, aur usse lagta tha ki school mein western science padhaya ja raha hai lekin God aur scriptures ke baare mein kuch nahi sikhaaya ja raha hai. Music lessons se toh woh aur bhi zyada pareshan ho gayi, kyunki usse music ke baare mein galat khayalat the, woh kehti thi ki music sirf randiyon aur bhikariyon ka kaam hai, gentle logon ke liye nahi hai.

original_instruction: What was the grandmother's happiest half-hour of the day when the narrator was at university?
original_input: Only in the afternoon she relaxed for a while to feed the sparrows. While she sat in the verandah breaking the bread into little bits, hundreds of little birds collected round her creating a veritable bedlam of chirrupings. Some came and perched on her legs, others on her shoulders. Some even sat on her head. She smiled but never shooed them away. It used to be the happiest half-hour of the day for her.
original_output: Her happiest half-hour of the day was in the afternoon when she relaxed to feed the sparrows. She would sit in the verandah, breaking bread into bits, and hundreds of birds would gather around her, perching on her legs, shoulders, and even head, creating a joyful commotion.
hinglish_question: Dadi ji ke liye din ka sabse khushiyon bhara adha ghanta ka samay kab hota tha jab narrator university mein hota tha? Sirf dopahar mein woh thodi der ke liye aaraam karti thi taaki chidiyon ko khana khilaye. Jab woh verandah mein baithkar bread ko chhote tukdon mein todti thi, toh hazaron chhote chhote pakshi uske aas paas ikattha ho jaate the, aur ek ajeeb tarah ki shor mach jaata tha. Kuch pakshi uske pairon par, kuch uske kandhe par, aur kuch toh uske sir par baith jaate the. Woh muskuraati thi lekin unhein kabhi bhi bhagaati nahi thi. Yeh uske liye din ka sabse khushiyon bhara adha ghanta hota tha.
hinglish_answer: Dadi ji ke liye din ka sabse khushiyon bhara adha ghanta ka samay dopahar mein hota tha jab woh aaraam karti thi aur chidiyon ko khana khilati thi. Woh verandah mein baithkar bread ko chhote tukdon mein todti thi, aur hazaron pakshi uske aas paas ikattha ho jaate the, uske pairon par, kandhe par, aur sir par baithkar ek ajeeb tarah ki khushi ka mahaul bana dete the.

original_instruction: What unusual activity did the grandmother engage in the evening before she fell ill?
original_input: In the evening a change came over her. She did not pray. She collected the women of the neighbourhood, got an old drum and started to sing. For several hours she thumped the sagging skins of the dilapidated drum and sang of the home-coming of warriors. We had to persuade her to stop to avoid overstraining. That was the first time since I had known her that she did not pray.
original_output: The evening before she fell ill, the grandmother did not pray, which was highly unusual for her. Instead, she gathered women from the neighborhood, found an old, dilapidated drum, and for several hours, she thumped it and sang songs about the home-coming of warriors, needing to be persuaded to stop.
hinglish_question: Dadi ji ne bimari se pehle shaam ko kya ajeeb kaam kiya tha? Shaam ko unmein kuch badlav aaya. Unhone prayer nahin ki. Unhone pados ki auraton ko ikattha kiya, purane dhol ko uthaya aur geet gaane lagein. Kayi ghanton tak unhone purane dhol ki dhilon ko peetkar geet gaaye, jo sipahiyo ke ghar vapas aane ke bare mein the. Humein unhe rokne ke liye manana pada, nahi toh unhe zyada tanav ho sakta tha. Yeh pehli baar tha jab se maine unhe jaana tha, ki unhone prayer nahin ki.
hinglish_answer: Bimari se pehle ki shaam ko, dadi ji ne prayer nahin ki, jo unke liye bahut hi ajeeb tha. Unhone pados ki auraton ko ikattha kiya, ek purana, kharaab dhol uthaya, aur kayi ghanton tak uspe thapki dete hue sipahiyo ke ghar vapas aane ke geet gaaye, aur humein unhe rokne ke liye manana pada.

original_instruction: According to custom, what was done with the grandmother's body after her death?
original_input: We lifted her off the bed and, as is customary, laid her on the ground and covered her with a red shroud.
original_output: As was customary, after her death, her body was lifted off the bed, laid on the ground, and covered with a red shroud.
hinglish_question: Riwaj ke hisab se dadi ji ki death ke baad unka body kya kiya gaya tha? Humne unhe bed se uthaya aur riwaj ke mutabik zameen par leta kar laal kapde se dhak diya.
hinglish_answer: Riwaj ke hisab se dadi ji ki death ke baad unka body bed se uthakar zameen par laya gaya aur laal kapde se dhak diya gaya.

original_instruction: What inspired the narrator and his wife, Mary, to embark on their round-the-world voyage?
original_input: In July 1976, my wife Mary, son Jonathan, 6, daughter Suzanne, 7, and I set sail from Plymouth, England, to duplicate the round-the-world voyage made 200 years earlier by Captain James Cook. For the longest time, Mary and I — a 37-year-old businessman — had dreamt of sailing in the wake of the famous explorer
original_output: The narrator and his wife, Mary, were inspired by Captain James Cook's 200-year-old round-the-world voyage and had dreamt of duplicating it for a long time.
hinglish_question: Kya cheez ne narrator aur uski wife Mary ko poora duniya ka safar karne ke liye prerit kiya? Yaani, unhone Captain James Cook ke 200 saal phele ke duniya bhar ka safar ko duplicate karne ke liye England se sail kiya tha
hinglish_answer: Narrator aur uski wife Mary ko Captain James Cook ke 200 saal purane duniya bhar ke safar ne inspire kiya tha, aur ve isko duplicate karne ke sapne dekhte aaye the

original_instruction: Describe the boat, Wavewalker, that the family used for their journey.
original_input: Our boat Wavewalker , a 23 metre, 30 ton wooden-hulled beauty, had been professionally built, and we had spent months fitting it out and testing it in the roughest weather we could find.
original_output: Wavewalker was a 23-meter, 30-ton wooden-hulled boat that had been professionally built. The family spent months fitting it out and testing it in the roughest weather.
hinglish_question: Wavewalker boat ke baare mein batao, jo family ne apne safar ke liye use kiya tha. Humari Wavewalker boat, 23 metre, 30 ton ka lakdi ke hull waali boat, professionally banayi gayi thi, aur humne mahino tak usse taiyar kiya aur sabse khatarnaak mausam mein test kiya tha.
hinglish_answer: Wavewalker 23 metre, 30 ton ka lakdi ke hull waali boat thi, jo professionally banayi gayi thi. Family ne mahino tak usse taiyar kiya aur sabse khatarnaak mausam mein test kiya tha.

original_instruction: Where did the family take on additional crew members and for what purpose?
original_input: The first leg of our planned three-year, 105,000 kilometre journey passed pleasantly as we sailed down the west coast of Africa to Cape Town. There, before heading east, we took on two crewmen — American Larry Vigil and Swiss Herb Seigler — to help us tackle one of the world’s roughest seas, the southern Indian Ocean.
original_output: The family took on two crewmen, American Larry Vigil and Swiss Herb Seigler, in Cape Town. Their purpose was to help tackle the notoriously rough Southern Indian Ocean.
hinglish_question: Parivaar ne kahaan aur kis uddeshya se naye crew members ko shaamil kiya?
hinglish_answer: Parivaar ne Cape Town mein American Larry Vigil aur Swiss Herb Seigler naamak do crewmen ko shaamil kiya, unka uddeshya southern Indian Ocean ko paar karna tha, jo duniya ke sabse khatarnaak samudron mein se ek hai

original_instruction: What significant event occurred at dawn on January 2 that led to the severe damage of the ship?
original_input: At dawn on January 2, the waves were gigantic... The first indication of impending disaster came at about 6 p.m., with an ominous silence. The wind dropped, and the sky immediately grew dark. Then came a growing roar, and an enormous cloud towered aft of the ship. With horror, I realised that it was not a cloud, but a wave like no other I had ever seen. It appeared perfectly vertical and almost twice the height of the other waves, with a frightful breaking crest. The roar increased to a thunder as the stern moved up the face of the wave, and for a moment I thought we might ride over it. But then a tremendous explosion shook the deck. A torrent of green and white water broke over the ship, my head smashed into the wheel and I was aware of flying overboard and sinking below the waves.
original_output: At dawn on January 2, the waves were gigantic, but the disaster struck around 6 p.m. with an enormous, perfectly vertical wave, almost twice the height of others, with a frightful breaking crest. This wave caused a tremendous explosion, breaking over the ship and severely damaging it, even throwing the narrator overboard.
hinglish_question: 2 January ki subah kya badi ghatna ghati thi jisne ship ko kharab kar diya? 2 January ki subah toh waves bahut bade the... lekin 6 baje ke karib kya hua tha?
hinglish_answer: 2 January ki subah waves toh bade the, lekin asal mein disaster 6 baje ke karib hua jab ek ajeeb sa, vertical wave aaya jo do guna bada tha, uska crest bhi bahut khatarnak tha. Is wave ne ship ko kharab kar diya, ek bada explosion hua aur narrator ko bhi paani mein fek diya.

original_instruction: What was the immediate aftermath and condition of Wavewalker and its crew after being hit by the massive wave?
original_input: A few metres away, Wavewalker was near capsizing, her masts almost horizontal... My left ribs cracked; my mouth filled with blood and broken teeth... “We’re sinking!” she screamed. “The decks are smashed; we’re full of water.” ...Larry and Herb were pumping like madmen. Broken timbers hung at crazy angles, the whole starboard side bulged inwards; clothes, crockery, charts, tins and toys sloshed about in deep water.
original_output: Wavewalker was near capsizing with its masts almost horizontal, and the decks were smashed, filling with water. The starboard side bulged inwards with broken timbers, and the narrator sustained cracked ribs, a mouth full of blood, and broken teeth. Larry and Herb immediately began pumping water.
hinglish_question: Wavewalker aur uske crew ke saath kya hua jab unhe massive wave ne hit kiya? Uske baad Wavewalker ki haalat kaisi thi?
hinglish_answer: Wavewalker capsizing ke karib thi, uske mast almost horizontal the, decks toh smash ho gaye the, aur paani se bhar gaye the. Starboard side andar ki taraf bulge ho gaya tha, broken timbers bhi the, aur narrator ke ribs crack ho gaye the, mouth mein blood aur broken teeth the. Larry aur Herb ne turant water pump karna shuru kar diya.

original_instruction: Describe the challenges the narrator faced while trying to manage the flooding and repair the ship after the disaster.
original_input: With the starboard side bashed open, we were taking water with each wave that broke over us. If I couldn’t make some repairs, we would surely sink. Somehow I managed to stretch canvas and secure waterproof hatch covers across the gaping holes. Some water continued to stream below, but most of it was now being deflected over the side. More problems arose when our hand pumps started to block up with the debris floating around the cabins and the electric pump short- circuited. The water level rose threateningly. Back on deck I found that our two spare hand pumps had been wrenched overboard — along with the forestay sail, the jib, the dinghies and the main anchor. Then I remembered we had another electric pump under the chartroom floor. I connected it to an out-pipe, and was thankful to find that it worked.
original_output: The narrator struggled to stretch canvas and secure waterproof hatch covers over gaping holes on the starboard side. Further challenges included hand pumps blocking with debris, the main electric pump short-circuiting, and two spare hand pumps being washed overboard. He eventually found and connected another electric pump from under the chartroom floor, which thankfully worked.
hinglish_question: Disaster ke baad ship ko repair karne aur flooding ko manage karne mein narrator ko kaun kaun se challenges ka saamna karna pada? Jab starboard side se paani andar aa raha tha, toh narrator ne kya kya kiya?
hinglish_answer: Narrator ko starboard side ke holes pe canvas stretch karna aur waterproof hatch covers secure karna bahut mushkil laga. Uske baad hand pumps block ho gaye, electric pump short-circuit ho gayi, aur do spare hand pumps bhi samundar mein gir gaye. Phir narrator ne chartroom ke neeche se ek aur electric pump dhundha aur use connect kiya, jo ki finally kaam kar gaya.

original_instruction: What act of courage did Suzanne (Sue) display, and what was her reason for it?
original_input: Sue’s head had swollen alarmingly; she had two enormous black eyes, and now she showed us a deep cut on her arm. When I asked why she hadn’t made more of her injuries before this, she replied, “I didn’t want to worry you when you were trying to save us all.”
original_output: Suzanne showed immense courage by not mentioning her alarming injuries, which included a swollen head, two enormous black eyes, and a deep cut on her arm, earlier. She explained that she didn't want to worry her father while he was trying to save them all.
hinglish_question: Suzanne ne kya sahas dikhaya aur uske peeche uska kya wajah thi? Uski head bohot zyada swole ho gayi thi, uske do bade black eyes the, aur ab usne humein apne arm par ek gahra cut bhi dikhaya. Maine jab pucha ki vah pehle apni injuries ke baare mein kyun nahi batayi, toh usne kaha, 'Maine socha ki main aapko worry nahi karana chahti jab aap hum sabko bachane ki koshish kar rahe the.'
hinglish_answer: Suzanne ne bohot sahas dikhaya jab usne apni injuries ke baare mein pehle nahi bataya, jisme uski swole head, do bade black eyes aur arm par ek gahra cut shaamil the. Usne samjhaya ki vah apne papa ko worry nahi karana chahti thi jab vah hum sabko bachane ki koshish kar rahe the.

original_instruction: After assessing the extensive damage to Wavewalker, what was the narrator's calculated hope for their survival?
original_input: But we still had a tremendous leak somewhere below the waterline and, on checking, I found that nearly all the boat’s main rib frames were smashed down to the keel. In fact, there was nothing holding up a whole section of the starboard hull except a few cupboard partitions. We had survived for 15 hours since the wave hit, but Wavewalker wouldn’t hold together long enough for us to reach Australia. I checked our charts and calculated that there were two small islands a few hundred kilometres to the east. One of them, Ile Amsterdam, was a French scientific base. Our only hope was to reach these pinpricks in the vast ocean.
original_output: The narrator's only hope for survival was to reach two small islands, Ile Amsterdam (a French scientific base) being one of them, located a few hundred kilometers to the east. He referred to these as "pinpricks in the vast ocean" because Wavewalker was too damaged to make it to Australia.
hinglish_question: Wavewalker ko itni badi damage hone ke baad, narrator ko apni survival ke liye kya ummeed thi? Humne dekha ki boat ke neeche paani ki line ke neeche ek bada leak tha, aur jab maine check kiya toh pata chala ki boat ke sabse bade rib frames keel tak smash ho gaye the. Asal mein, starboard hull ka ek pura section sirf kuch cupboard partitions se uthaya hua tha. Hum wave ke hit hone ke 15 ghante tak zinda the, lekin Wavewalker itna lamba nahi chalega ki hum Australia tak pahunch sake. Maine apne charts check kiye aur dekha ki east mein kuch hundred kilometre door do chhote islands hain. Unmein se ek, Ile Amsterdam, ek French scientific base tha. Humari ekmatr ummeed yeh thi ki hum in chhoti chhoti islands tak pahunch sake, jo ki ek bade samundar mein sirf pinpricks jaise thi.
hinglish_answer: Narrator ki sirf ek ummeed thi ki wo do chhote islands tak pahunch sake, jismein se ek Ile Amsterdam tha, jo ki ek French scientific base tha, jo ki kuch hundred kilometre east mein tha. Unhone inhein 'vast ocean ke pinpricks' kaha kyunki Wavewalker itna damaged tha ki Australia tak nahi pahunch sakta tha.

original_instruction: Explain the meaning of the expression "pinpricks in the vast ocean" as used in the text.
original_input: Our only hope was to reach these pinpricks in the vast ocean.
original_output: The expression "pinpricks in the vast ocean" refers to the two small islands, including Ile Amsterdam, that were the family's only hope for survival. It emphasizes their tiny size and remoteness in the immense and dangerous ocean, highlighting how difficult they would be to find.
hinglish_question: yeh expression 'pinpricks in the vast ocean' ka kya matlab hai, jo ki text me use hua hai? Hamara bas ek hope tha ki hum in pinpricks in the vast ocean tak pahuch paye
hinglish_answer: yeh expression 'pinpricks in the vast ocean' do chhote islands ko refer karta hai, jisme se ek Ile Amsterdam hai, jo family ke liye bas ek hope tha for survival. Yeh unke chhoti size aur remoteness ko emphasize karta hai immense and dangerous ocean me, jo ki unhe find karna bohot mushkil banata hai

original_instruction: What profound statement did Jonathan make to his father when asked about their chances of survival on January 5?
original_input: When I went in to comfort the children, Jon asked, “Daddy, are we going to die?” I tried to assure him that we could make it. “But, Daddy,” he went on, “we aren’t afraid of dying if we can all be together — you and Mummy, Sue and I.”
original_output: Jonathan told his father, "we aren’t afraid of dying if we can all be together — you and Mummy, Sue and I." This statement conveyed his courage and the family's unity in the face of impending death.
hinglish_question: Jonathan ne apne papa se 5 January ko jab unse poocha gaya ki unki survival ke chances kya hain, toh usne kya kahaa?
hinglish_answer: Jonathan ne kaha, 'humein marne ka dar nahi hai agar hum sab saath ho - tum, mummy, sue aur main'. Is statement se unki himmat aur parivaar ki ekta dikhayi di

original_instruction: Who discovered King Tutankhamun's tomb and in what year?

original_input: The ritual resins had hardened, cementing Tut to the bottom of his solid gold coffin. “No amount of legitimate force could move them,” Carter wrote later. ...the consolidated material had to be chiselled away from beneath the limbs and trunk before it was possible to raise the king’s remains.

hinglish_answer: Howard Carter ko problem yeh thi ki ritual resins solid ho gaye the aur Tutankhamun ki mummy uske solid gold coffin ke neeche cemented ho gayi thi, jiske kaaran usse koi bhi force lagane se mummy hila nahi rahi thi, toh phir usne consolidated material ko chisel karke mummy ke limbs aur trunk ke neeche se nikalna pada taki king ka body uthaya ja sake.

original_output: King Tut was buried with everyday items for the afterlife, including board games, a bronze razor, linen undergarments, and cases of food and wine.

original_instruction: What evidence suggested the season of King Tut's burial?

original_output: A shroud adorned with garlands of willow and olive leaves, wild celery, lotus petals, and cornflowers provided faded evidence that King Tut's burial took place in March or April.

original_output: An X-ray in 1968 revealed that King Tut's breast-bone and front ribs were missing from beneath the resin caking his chest.
hinglish_question: King Tut ki mummy ke baare mein 1968 mein X-ray examination se kya chaukane wala fact pata chala? 1968 mein, Carter ke discovery ke 40 saal ke baad, ek anatomy professor ne mummy ki X-ray ki aur ek chaukane wala fact reveal kiya: resin ke neeche, uske chest ke andar, uska breast-bone aur front ribs gayab hain.
hinglish_answer: 1968 mein X-ray se pata chala ki King Tut ke paas resin ke neeche chest ke andar breast-bone aur front ribs nahi hain.

original_instruction: Who was Akhenaten, and what significant religious and political changes did he implement during his reign?
original_input: His son Amenhotep IV succeeded him and initiated one of the strangest periods in the history of ancient Egypt. The new pharaoh promoted the worship of the Aten, the sun disk, changed his name to Akhenaten, or ‘servant of the Aten,’ and moved the religious capital from the old city of Thebes to the new city of Akhetaten, known now as Amarna. He further shocked the country by attacking Amun, a major god, smashing his images and closing his temples.
original_output: Akhenaten, originally Amenhotep IV, promoted the worship of the Aten (sun disk), changed his name to 'servant of the Aten,' moved the religious capital to Akhetaten (Amarna), and attacked the major god Amun by smashing his images and closing his temples.
hinglish_question: Akhenaten kaun tha, aur usne apne rajya mein kya mahatvapoorn dharmik aur rajnaitik parivartan kiye? Uske bete Amenhotep IV ne usey succeed kiya aur pracheen misr ke itihas mein sabse ajeeb samay ki shuruaat ki. Naye pharaoh ne Aten, sun disk ki pooja ko badhava diya, apna naam Akhenaten, ya 'aten ka sewak' rakha, aur dharmik rajdhani ko purane shahar Thebes se naye shahar Akhetaten, jo ab Amarna ke roop mein jana jata hai, shift kar diya. Usne desh ko aur bhi shock kiya jab usne bade devta Amun par hamla kiya, uske chitra tod diye aur uske mandir band kar diye.
hinglish_answer: Akhenaten, jo pehle Amenhotep IV tha, usne Aten (sun disk) ki pooja ko badhava diya, apna naam 'aten ka sewak' rakha, dharmik rajdhani ko Akhetaten (Amarna) shift kiya, aur bade devta Amun par hamla kiya, uske chitra tod kar aur uske mandir band karke.

original_instruction: When did the Egyptian Mummy Project begin its inventory, and what is its next planned phase?

original_output: The Egyptian Mummy Project began its inventory in late 2003. Its next phase is to scan the mummies using a portable CT machine donated by the National Geographic Society and Siemens.

Agla phase: ek portable CT machine se mummy ki scanning karna, jo National Geographic Society aur Siemens, uske manufacturer ne donate kiya hai.
hinglish_answer: Egyptian Mummy Project ne apna inventory 2003 ke end me shuru kiya. Uska agla phase hai ki woh portable CT machine ka use karke mummy ki scanning kare, jo National Geographic Society aur Siemens ne donate kiya hai.

original_instruction: How did Howard Carter justify his drastic actions of chiseling and dissecting Tutankhamun's mummy?

original_instruction: When did the Green Movement begin, and what significant event occurred shortly after its inception?

hinglish_answer: Green Movement lagbhag 25 saal pehle 1994 se shuru hua tha (karib 1969 mein). 1972 mein, duniya ki pehli nationwide Green party New Zealand mein banayi gayi thi.

original_instruction: According to the World Commission on Environment and Development, how is 'sustainable development' defined?
original_input: The concept of sustainable development was popularised in 1987 by the World Commission on Environment and Development. In its report it defined the idea as “Development that meets the needs of the present, without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs”, i.e., without stripping the natural world of resources future generations would need.
original_output: Sustainable development is defined as 'Development that meets the needs of the present, without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs,' meaning it involves using resources without stripping the natural world of what future generations would need.
hinglish_question: World Commission on Environment and Development ke hisab se, sustainable development ka definition kya hai? hinglish_answer: Sustainable development ka definition hai ki yeh development hai jo present ke needs ko pura karta hai, lekin future generations ke needs ko compromise karte hue nahi, matlab ki hum resources ka use karte hain lekin future generations ke liye zaruri cheezein natural world se hataye nahi

original_instruction: What is the significance of the notice in the Lusaka, Zambia zoo cage that reads 'The world’s most dangerous animal'?
original_input: In the zoo at Lusaka, Zambia, there is a cage where the notice reads, ‘The world’s most dangerous animal’. Inside the cage there is no animal but a mirror where you see yourself. original_instruction: How was the political structure of India described in the twentieth century in the history book Professor Gaitonde read?
original_input: The twentieth century brought about further changes inspired by the West. India moved towards a democracy. By then, the Peshwas had lost their enterprise and they were gradually replaced by democratically elected bodies. The Sultanate at Delhi survived even this transition, largely because it wielded no real influence. The Shahenshah of Delhi was no more than a figurehead to rubber-stamp the ‘recommendations’ made by the central parliament.
original_output: In the twentieth century, India moved towards a democracy, with the Peshwas being replaced by democratically elected bodies. The Sultanate at Delhi survived, but the Shahenshah was merely a figurehead who rubber-stamped recommendations from the central parliament.
hinglish_question: Professor Gaitonde ne jo history book padha tha usmein 20th century mein India ki political structure kaise describe ki gayi thi? Tab West se inspire hokar kuch aur changes aaye the, India democracy ki taraf badhne laga. Tab tak Peshwa log apni capability kho chuke the aur unki jagah democratically elected bodies ne le li thi. Delhi ka Sultanate bhi is transition mein survive kar gaya, kyunki uska asal mein koi influence nahi tha. Delhi ka Shahenshah sirf ek figurehead tha jo central parliament ke 'suggestions' par rubber-stamp karta tha.
hinglish_answer: 20th century mein India democracy ki taraf badhne laga, Peshwa log democratically elected bodies se replace ho gaye. Delhi ka Sultanate survive kar gaya lekin Shahenshah sirf ek figurehead tha jo central parliament ke recommendations ko rubber-stamp karta tha.

original_instruction: What type of wild animals did the travelers encounter on the plains, and how did they behave?
original_input: Further on, where the plains became more stony than grassy, a great herd of wild ass came into view. Tsetan told us we were approaching them long before they appeared. When we drew near, I could see the herd galloping en masse, wheeling and turning in tight formation as if they were practising manoeuvres on some predetermined course.
original_output: They encountered a great herd of wild ass, called Kyang, which were seen galloping en masse, wheeling and turning in tight formation, creating plumes of dust.
hinglish_question: Plains mein traveler ko kaun kaun se wild animals milte hai, aur ve kaise behave karte hai? Agar plains mein stone zyada ho aur ghaas kam ho, toh kya hota hai?
hinglish_answer: Unhe ek bada herd mila wild ass ka, jo kyang kehte hai, jo mass mein bhagte hue, wheeling aur turning karte hue tight formation mein dekhe gaye, jaise ki ve kisi predetermined course par manoeuvres practice kar rahe ho

original_instruction: What was the typical behavior of the Tibetan mastiffs guarding the nomads' tents as the vehicle approached?
original_input: These beasts would cock their great big heads when they became aware of our approach and fix us in their sights. As we continued to draw closer, they would explode into action, speeding directly towards us, like a bullet from a gun and nearly as fast. These shaggy monsters, blacker than the darkest night, usually wore bright red collars and barked furiously with massive jaws. They were completely fearless of our vehicle, shooting straight into our path, causing Tsetan to brake and swerve.
original_output: As the vehicle approached, the Tibetan mastiffs would cock their heads, fix the car in their sights, then explode into action, speeding directly towards it, barking furiously and forcing Tsetan to brake and swerve.
hinglish_question: Nomads ke tent ke paas wale Tibetan mastiffs ka kya behaviour hota tha jab vehicle aati thi? Ye beasts apne bade heads ko cock karte the jab unhe pata chalta tha ki hum aarahe hain, phir ve hume apni nazar mein le lete the. Jab hum aur paas aate the, ve action mein aajate the, humari taraf se seedha tezi se aate the, jaise ki gun se nikla hua goli, aur utni hi tez. Ye shaggy monsters, jo ki sabse andhere raat se bhi zyada kaale hote the, aam taur par laal collars pehante hote the aur apne bade jaws ke saath bhukk bhukk karte the. Ve hamein apni gaadi se bilkul nahi darte the, seedha humari raah mein aa jaate the, jisse Tsetan ko brake aur swerve karna padta tha.
hinglish_answer: Jab vehicle aati thi, Tibetan mastiffs apne heads ko cock karte the, gaadi ko apni nazar mein le lete the, phir action mein aajate the, seedha uski taraf tezi se aate the, bhukk bhukk karte the aur Tsetan ko brake aur swerve karne ke liye majboor karte the.

original_instruction: How did Tsetan, Daniel, and the narrator overcome the first snow blockage on the track?
original_input: A swathe of the white stuff lay across the track in front of us, stretching for maybe fifteen metres... Tsetan stepped on to the encrusted snow and began to slither and slide forward, stamping his foot... 'If we slip off, the car could turn over,' he suggested, as we saw Tsetan grab handfuls of dirt and fling them across the frozen surface. We both pitched in and, when the snow was spread with soil, Daniel and I stayed out of the vehicle to lighten Tsetan’s load. He backed up and drove towards the dirty snow, eased the car on to its icy surface and slowly drove its length without apparent difficulty.
original_output: Tsetan, Daniel, and the narrator spread dirt over the icy snow patch to create traction. Daniel and the narrator then exited the vehicle to lighten its load, allowing Tsetan to slowly drive the car across the dirt-covered snow.
hinglish_question: Tsetan, Daniel aur narrator ne track pe pehli baar snow blockage ko kaise cross kiya? Saamne hamare samne lagbhag pandrah metre tak white snow thi... Tsetan ne encrusted snow par foot rakha aur slip karke aage badhne laga, apna foot stamp karta hua... 'Agar hum slip ho jaate hain, to car ulat sakta hai,' Tsetan ne suggest kiya, jab humne use mitti ke handfuls uthate aur frozen surface par daalate hue dekha. Hum dono ne bhi madad ki, aur jab snow par mitti daali gayi, to Daniel aur main vehicle se bahar utar gaye taaki Tsetan ka load lightweight ho jaaye. Tsetan ne car ko reverse kiya aur dirty snow ki taraf drive kiya, car ko uske icy surface par rakha aur dheere se uski length tak bina kisi mushkil ke drive kiya.
hinglish_answer: Tsetan, Daniel aur narrator ne icy snow patch par mitti daal kar traction create ki. Phir Daniel aur narrator vehicle se utar gaye taaki Tsetan ka load lightweight ho jaaye, aur Tsetan ne car ko dheere se dirt-covered snow par drive kiya.

original_instruction: What was the elevation of the pass summit, and what traditional markers were found there?

original_output: The pass summit was at 5,515 metres and was marked by a large cairn of rocks adorned with white silk scarves and ragged prayer flags.

hinglish_answer: Pass summit 5,515 metres par tha, aur yeh ek bade cairn of rocks se marked tha, jahan white silk scarves aur ragged prayer flags lage hue the.

original_instruction: What effect did the lower atmospheric pressure at the high altitude have on the vehicle's fuel tank, and how did Tsetan react?
original_input: He stopped at the petrol tank and partially unscrewed the top, which emitted a loud hiss. The lower atmospheric pressure was allowing the fuel to expand. It sounded dangerous to me. 'Maybe, sir,' Tsetan laughed 'but no smoking.'
original_output: The lower atmospheric pressure caused the fuel in the petrol tank to expand, emitting a loud hiss when Tsetan partially unscrewed the top. Tsetan acknowledged the potential danger but laughed it off, simply advising "no smoking."
hinglish_question: High altitude par lower atmospheric pressure ne vehicle ke fuel tank pe kya effect kiya, aur Tsetan ne kaisa react kiya? Vah petrol tank ke paas ruk gaya aur top ko partially unscrew kiya, jiske baad ek loud hiss sunai di. Lower atmospheric pressure ke kaaran fuel expand ho raha tha. Mujhe lagta hai ki yeh khatarnaak tha. 'Shayad, sir,' Tsetan hansne laga 'lekin smoking mat karna.
hinglish_answer: Lower atmospheric pressure ke kaaran fuel tank me fuel expand ho gaya, jab Tsetan ne top ko partially unscrew kiya to loud hiss sunai di. Tsetan ne potential danger ko acknowledge kiya lekin hans ke taal di, sirf 'smoking mat karna' advise kiya.

original_instruction: Where did the travelers stop for lunch after descending the pass, and what kind of activity was happening there?
original_input: It was two o’clock by the time we stopped for lunch. We ate hot noodles inside a long canvas tent, part of a workcamp erected beside a dry salt lake. The plateau is pockmarked with salt flats and brackish lakes, vestiges of the Tethys Ocean... This one was a hive of activity, men with pickaxes and shovels trudging back and forth in their long sheepskin coats and salt-encrusted boots. All wore sunglasses against the glare as a steady stream of blue trucks emerged from the blindingly white lake laden with piles of salt.
original_output: They stopped for lunch at a workcamp beside a dry salt lake. The camp was a hive of activity, with men digging salt with pickaxes and shovels, and blue trucks continuously emerging from the lake laden with salt.
hinglish_question: Pass utarte hue lunch kahan par rukke aur wahan kya ho raha tha?
hinglish_answer: Unhone lunch ek workcamp me liya jo ek sukhe namak ke talab ke paas tha. Wahan bahut activity ho rahi thi, aadmi pickaxes aur phavde lekar namak khod rahe the, aur blue trucks lagatar talab se namak bhare hue nikal rahe the.

original_instruction: Why and where did Daniel part ways with the narrator and Tsetan?
original_input: By late afternoon we had reached the small town of Hor, back on the main east-west highway that followed the old trade route from Lhasa to Kashmir. Daniel, who was returning to Lhasa, found a ride in a truck so Tsetan and I bade him farewell outside a tyre-repair shop.
original_output: Daniel, who was returning to Lhasa, found a ride in a truck in the small town of Hor, where he parted ways with the narrator and Tsetan outside a tyre-repair shop.
hinglish_question: Daniel aur narrator aur Tsetan kab aur kahan alag hue? Daniel, jo ki Lhasa wapas ja raha tha, usne ek truck mein ride dhundh li, toh Tsetan aur maine use ek tyre-repair shop ke bahar bidai di.
hinglish_answer: Daniel, jo ki Lhasa wapas ja raha tha, usne Hor shahar mein ek truck mein ride dhundh li, jahan usne narrator aur Tsetan se alag hokar ek tyre-repair shop ke bahar bidai li.

original_instruction: How should information be logically divided and subdivided in good notes?
original_input: Information is logically divided and subdivided by the use of figures/letters. The divisions are made like this: Main sections : 1, 2, 3, etc. Sub-sections : (i), (ii), (iii), etc. Sub-sub-sections : (a), (b), (c), etc.
original_output: In good notes, information is logically divided and subdivided using figures/letters. Main sections are numbered 1, 2, 3, etc., sub-sections use (i), (ii), (iii), etc., and sub-sub-sections use (a), (b), (c), etc.
hinglish_question: Acchi notes mein information ko logically kaise divide aur sub-divide karna chahiye? Information ko logically divide aur sub-divide karne ke liye figures/letters ka use hota hai. Divisions is tarah se ki jati hain: Main sections - 1, 2, 3, etc. Sub-sections - (i), (ii), (iii), etc. Sub-sub-sections - (a), (b), (c), etc.
hinglish_answer: Acchi notes mein, information ko logically divide aur sub-divide karne ke liye figures/letters ka use kiya jata hai. Main sections ko 1, 2, 3, etc. number diya jata hai, sub-sections mein (i), (ii), (iii), etc. ka use hota hai, aur sub-sub-sections mein (a), (b), (c), etc. ka use kiya jata hai.

original_instruction: Explain the 'decimal' system for structuring notes.
original_input: Another common method is the ‘decimal’ system. Main sections : 1, 2, 3, etc. Sub-sections : 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, etc. Sub-sub-sections : 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.1.3, 1.2.1, 1.2.2, etc.
original_output: The 'decimal' system for structuring notes uses numbers like 1, 2, 3 for main sections; 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 for sub-sections; and 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.1.3, etc., for sub-sub-sections.
hinglish_question: Notes ko structure karne ke liye 'decimal' system ko explain karo. Isme main sections ke liye 1, 2, 3 number use hote hain, sub-sections ke liye 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, aur sub-sub-sections ke liye 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.1.3, 1.2.1, 1.2.2, etc. use hote hain.
hinglish_answer: Decimal system notes ko structure karne ka ek tarika hai, jisme main sections ke liye 1, 2, 3 number use hote hain, sub-sections ke liye 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, aur sub-sub-sections ke liye 1.1.1, 1.1.2, 1.1.3, etc. use hote hain.

original_instruction: Briefly explain how dead plant and animal material was preserved and transformed into coal and petroleum.
original_input: When these organisms died, much of their tissue was recycled as it is today — through scavenging and decay. But a significant amount of dead plant and animal material was covered with mud, which prevented complete decomposition. With the passage of time, layer upon layer of the fine sediment was deposited over the once-living material; the sheer weight turned the sediments to rock. Sandwiched between the layers, both coal and petroleum were produced and preserved under pressure.
original_output: Dead plant and animal material was covered with mud, preventing complete decomposition. Over time, layers of sediment were deposited, and the immense weight turned these sediments into rock. Under this pressure, sandwiched between the layers, coal and petroleum were produced and preserved.
hinglish_question: Dead plants aur animals ke material ko kaise preserve kiya gaya aur coal aur petroleum mein convert kiya gaya? Jab ye organisms mar gaye, toh unke tissue ka bahut sa hissa aaj ke tarah recycle ho gaya - scavenging aur decay ke through. Lekin dead plant aur animal material ka ek bada hissa mud se dhak gaya, jisne complete decomposition ko rok diya. Samay ke saath, fine sediment ke layer upon layer is once-living material ke oopar deposit ho gaye; sheer weight ne sediments ko rock mein badal diya. Layers ke beech mein, coal aur petroleum produce huye aur pressure ke neeche preserve ho gaye.
hinglish_answer: Dead plant aur animal material mud se dhak gaya, jisne complete decomposition ko rok diya. Samay ke saath, sediment ke layers deposit hote gaye, aur immense weight ne in sediments ko rock mein badal diya. Is pressure ke neeche, layers ke beech mein coal aur petroleum produce aur preserve ho gaye.

hinglish_answer: Summarising ka primary purpose original source ke main points report karna hai

original_instruction: How does summarising differ from note-making in terms of length and purpose?

original_output: Summarising is not as severely shortened as note-making. Note-making is usually for personal reference, while summarising is for reporting main points.

hinglish_answer: Summarising note-making jaise itna shortened nahi hota. Note-making usually personal reference ke liye hota hai, jabki summarising main points report karne ke liye hota hai.

original_instruction: What are the key steps involved in the process of summarising, after analyzing the passage?
original_input: The process of summarising would involve the steps followed in note-making: 1. underlining important ideas 2. writing them down, abridging the verbs 3. avoiding examples, explanations, repetition. However, instead of nominalising the points (changing verbs into nouns), we expand the points into full sentences and link them using suitable connectors.

hinglish_question: Passage ko analyse karne ke baad summarise karne ka process kya hota hai? Lekin nominalising ke bajaye hum points ko full sentences mein expand karte hain aur suitable connectors se link karte hain.
hinglish_answer: Key steps hain important ideas ko underline karna, verbs ko short karke unhein likhna, examples, explanations, aur repetition ko avoid karna. Phir nominalising ke bajaye points ko full sentences mein expand karna aur suitable connectors se link karna.

hinglish_answer: Soyabean legume family mein aate hain aur inhe alag-alag tarah ke soils pe aur kayi tarah ke climates mein ugaya ja sakta hai.

original_instruction: List several diverse uses of soybeans, including both food and non-food applications.

original_instruction: What natural phenomenon is identified as the cause of the Sahara's past 'green' period and its subsequent desertification?
original_input: The green Sahara was the product of the migration of the paleo-monsoon. In the same way that ice ages come and go, so too do monsoons migrate north and south. The dynamics of earth’s motion are responsible. The tilt of the earth’s axis varies in a regular cycle — sometimes the planet is more tilted towards the sun, sometimes less so. The axis also wobbles like a spinning top. The date of the earth’s perihelion — its closest approach to the sun — varies in a cycle as well. At times when the Northern Hemisphere tilts sharply towards the sun and the planet makes its closest approach, the increased blast of sunlight during the north’s summer months can cause the African monsoon... to shift to the north... Around 5,000 years ago the monsoon shifted dramatically southward again.
original_output: The migration of the paleo-monsoon, driven by the dynamics of Earth's motion including variations in axial tilt and perihelion, caused the Sahara's climate shifts. A northward shift of the monsoon led to the 'green' period, while a southward shift resulted in desertification.
hinglish_question: Sahara ke pehle ke 'green' period aur uske baad ki desertification ka kaaran konsi natural phenomenon hai? Sahara ki green period paleo-monsoon ki migration ke kaaran hui thi, jismein earth ki motion ka bhi role tha.
hinglish_answer: Paleo-monsoon ki migration, jo earth ki motion ke dynamics, axial tilt aur perihelion ke variations se driven thi, ne Sahara ke climate shifts ka kaaran banaya. Monsoon ki northward shift se 'green' period aaya, jabki southward shift se desertification hui.

original_instruction: Name four characteristics that define a good essay.
original_input: The characteristics of a good essay are: Unity : The essay should deal with the main subject, and all parts of it should be clearly linked with that subject. Coherence : There should be a logical sequence of thought. This requires a logical relationship between ideas, sentences and paragraphs. Relevance : Unimportant information should not be included. Proportion : Giving more space to the important ideas.
original_output: A good essay is characterized by Unity, Coherence, Relevance, and Proportion.

Coherence bhi honi chahiye, jismein vicharon, vaakyon aur anshon ke beech tarkeek kram hona chahiye. Relevance bhi zaroori hai, jismein avashyak jaankari hi shaamil honi chahiye. Aur Proportion bhi honi chahiye, jismein mahatvapoorn vicharon ko adhik jagah deni chahiye.
hinglish_answer: Ek achhe essay ki khubiyan hain Unity, Coherence, Relevance aur Proportion.

original_instruction: How should one address a total stranger in a formal letter, and what if you know their title but not personally?
original_input: 4. Mode of address or salutation Salutation is the mode of addressing a person. We may have the following forms. (i) Dear Sir/Madam (when we are writing to a total stranger whom we do not know at all). (ii) Dear Mr/Ms/Dr/Professor + Surname as in: Dear Dr Sinha, (when it is a formal relationship with the addressee and the writer does not know him or her personally).
original_output: When writing to a total stranger, the appropriate salutation is "Dear Sir/Madam." If you have a formal relationship with the addressee and know their title and surname (e.g., Mr, Ms, Dr, Professor), but not them personally, you should use "Dear Mr/Ms/Dr/Professor + Surname," such as "Dear Dr Sinha."

hinglish_answer: Kisi total stranger ko letter likhne mein 'Dear Sir/Madam' likhna thik rahega. Agar humein unka title pata hai, jaise ki Mr, Ms, Dr, Professor, aur surname bhi pata hai, lekin hum unhein personally nahin jaante, toh 'Dear Mr/Ms/Dr/Professor + Surname' likhna chahiye, jaise ki 'Dear Dr Sinha'.

original_instruction: What are some common expressions to avoid when starting or ending letters?
original_input: Do not begin your letters with hackneyed expressions like, ‘With reference to your letter dated 10 January’. Instead, use personalised variations like, ‘I was glad to receive your letter of 10 January…’ or ‘We were happy to note from your letter that the goods have reached you safely…’  Never end your letters with hanging participles like ‘Thanking you’ or ‘Awaiting your reply’. Instead write, ‘Thank you’ or ‘We/I await/ look forward to your reply’.
original_output: When starting a letter, avoid hackneyed expressions like "With reference to your letter dated 10 January." Instead, use personalized variations such as "I was glad to receive your letter of 10 January…" When ending a letter, never use hanging participles like "Thanking you" or "Awaiting your reply." Instead, write "Thank you" or "We/I await/look forward to your reply."

Iske bajaye hum 'I was glad to receive your letter of 10 January…' ya 'We were happy to note from your letter that the goods have reached you safely…' jaise personalised variations use kar sakte hai. Aur letters ko 'Thanking you' ya 'Awaiting your reply' jaise hanging participles se end nahi karna chahiye, iske bajaye hum 'Thank you' ya 'We/I await/ look forward to your reply' likh sakte hai.
hinglish_answer: Letter start karte waqt humen 'With reference to your letter dated 10 January' jaise hackneyed expressions se bachna chahiye.
